stories.headline: Netanyahu says Flydubai flight attacker 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination'
stories.summary: Netanyahu characterizes the Flydubai flight attacker as having undergone radicalization, framing the incident through a security and ideological lens ahead of upcoming Israeli elections. The attack, which involved a pilot being stabbed during a flight to Israel, raises broader questions about aviation safety protocols when crew members pose threats.

stories.headline: Tennessee halts executions after Christa Pike survives two lethal injection attempts
stories.summary: Tennessee has suspended its execution protocol after Christa Pike survived two separate lethal injection attempts on March 20, prompting state officials to review procedures that failed to administer a fatal dose. The halt affects all scheduled executions in the state and raises questions about how the department will proceed with Pike's case and whether systemic changes to the lethal injection process are necessary.

stories.headline: Russia targets busy bridge in central Kyiv
stories.summary: Russian forces launched strikes against infrastructure and civilian targets in Kyiv, including a central bridge and a school, as part of an intensified aerial campaign. Ukraine continues to face pressure from sustained attacks on both military and civilian sites across the capital.

stories.headline: Fires break out at French schools as students protest nationwide
stories.summary: Student protests across France have escalated to include fires and blockades at schools, prompting authorities to make hundreds of arrests as the unrest spreads to university campuses. The demonstrations center on education conditions and reflect broader frustrations among young people that extend beyond individual schools.

stories.headline: Zimbabwe businessman Wicknell Chivayo killed in helicopter crash
stories.summary: Wicknell Chivayo, a prominent Zimbabwean businessman with interests in mining and telecommunications, died in a helicopter crash along with his wife. Authorities have launched an investigation into the incident as the business community and public respond to the loss of one of the country's most visible entrepreneurs.

stories.headline: UK PM Burnham says Iran likely behind RAF base incident: Is there evidence?
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Burnham attributes a suspected incident at RAF Fairford to Iran based on what he describes as strong indications, though he has not publicly detailed specific evidence supporting the assessment. Iran denies involvement and has summoned the British envoy to protest what it calls false accusations, while Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu claims Israel had previously warned the UK of a potential Iranian attack.

stories.headline: Blasts heard in Addis Ababa as Ethiopia conflict widens in the north
stories.summary: Explosions have been reported in Ethiopia's capital Addis Ababa as fighting between federal forces and northern armed groups intensifies in the Tigray region and surrounding areas. The escalation is blocking humanitarian access to millions of civilians and creating severe shortages of food, medicine, and basic services across northern Ethiopia.

stories.headline: Family of Renee Good sues ICE agent who shot her and top Trump officials
stories.summary: The family of Renee Good has filed a lawsuit against an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent and senior Trump administration officials following her fatal shooting in Minneapolis. The case centers on circumstances surrounding Good's death during an interaction with federal immigration authorities.

stories.headline: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
stories.summary: Swiss glaciers lost more than 5% of their ice volume in 2026, marking the second-largest annual melt on record and continuing a dramatic acceleration in ice loss. Over the past five years, the country's glaciers have shrunk by roughly 20%, a pace that reflects sustained warming across the Alpine region.

stories.headline: Global bond sell-off intensifies, as UK long-term borrowing costs pass 6%
stories.summary: UK long-term borrowing costs have exceeded 6% as investors worldwide move out of bonds, reflecting rising expectations for higher interest rates and inflation concerns. The sell-off extends globally, with US Treasury yields reaching their highest levels in over two decades.
